name: Modern PHP (8.3+)
description: Enforces PHP 8.3 patterns including strict types, named arguments, enums, and readonly properties.
content:
# Modern PHP (8.3+) Rules

- Always declare `declare(strict_types=1)` at the top of every PHP file — no implicit type coercion
- Use typed properties and constructor promotion — `public function __construct(private readonly string $name)`
- Use native enums (`enum Status: string`) instead of class constants for fixed value sets
- Use named arguments for functions with many parameters — `array_slice(array: $data, offset: 2, length: 5)`
- Use `match` expressions instead of `switch` — they are strict, return values, and don't fall through
- Use union types (`string|int`) and intersection types (`Countable&Iterator`) in function signatures
- Use `readonly` classes and properties for immutable value objects — prevents accidental mutation
- Use fibers for cooperative multitasking in async workloads instead of callbacks
- Use `#[Attribute]` syntax for metadata instead of docblock annotations
- Prefer first-class callable syntax `strlen(...)` when passing functions as arguments
- Use `json_validate()` to check JSON before decoding — avoid silent failures from `json_decode`
- Run PHPStan at level 9 or Psalm at errorLevel 1 in CI — catch type errors before production
